sections.skill: Tell conversation context from saved memory

questions.prompt: In one chat, you mention your dog's name, and later in the same chat the model uses it. What makes this possible?

choices.text: The earlier message is still in the chat context
The model was retrained on your dog's name
The model guessed the name from training data
Every model knows every pet's name

questions.correct_answer: The earlier message is still in the chat context
questions.intro: Two different things can make a chatbot seem to "remember." CONVERSATION CONTEXT is the text of the current chat that is sent back to the model with each message, so it can refer to what you said earlier in that chat. SAVED MEMORY (or history features) is something a PRODUCT may offer: it stores notes or past chats and adds them to future conversations. Saved memory is a product feature, it varies between products, and it can usually be viewed, turned off or deleted in settings. Neither one retrains the model. Check what a specific product saves rather than assuming.
questions.feedback: Earlier messages in the chat are part of the context.

sections.skill: Compare a conversation with a notebook

questions.prompt: Saying "the movie I mentioned" during lunch is like what?

choices.text: A web search
Conversation context
Saved memory
Training a new model

questions.correct_answer: Conversation context
questions.intro: Talking to a friend at lunch, you can say "the movie I mentioned" because it came up a few minutes ago: that is like CONVERSATION CONTEXT. If your friend also keeps a NOTEBOOK and writes "likes horror movies," then next month they can bring it up again: that is like SAVED MEMORY. The notebook is something extra that your friend chose to keep, could show you, and could erase. Neither the lunch talk nor the notebook changes who your friend fundamentally is, just as neither one retrains a model.

sections.title: Apply it

questions.prompt: A family shares one account, and a new answer mentions a private detail one member shared. What is the issue?

choices.text: The model hacked the family's computer
Memory features never store private details
This is impossible with any product
Saved memory on a shared account can expose details

questions.correct_answer: Saved memory on a shared account can expose details
questions.intro: Memory features raise practical questions. Something you mentioned weeks ago could appear in a new answer, which may be helpful or unwelcome. Shared devices or shared accounts can expose saved notes to other people. Turning off memory may not delete chats already stored, and deleting a chat may not remove information a product saved separately; read what each setting actually does. For sensitive topics, the safest habit is not to share details you would not want stored, whatever the settings say.
questions.feedback: Shared accounts plus memory can leak details.
